title: Prevention, sharing well and your family action plan

say: Prevention, sharing well, and your family health action plan.
This is the video for module 3 of Maternal and Child Health Literacy.
Module 2 was about what to do when danger appears. This module is about stopping illness before it starts. Small habits add up.

say: WHO calls vaccines the most effective way to prevent pneumonia. Your guide is not a poster or a WhatsApp message. It is the child's own vaccination card. Bring it to every visit.

panel.heading: The card is your guide
items: Bring the card to every visit
Check each dose is written down
Ask: when is the next one?
Save the date with a reminder
Photograph the card

say: After each dose, check it was written on the card, and ask when the next one is due.

say: Save the next date in your phone with a reminder two days before.

say: Keep the card in a plastic sleeve and photograph it. And if a date is missed, go to the clinic as soon as possible. Do not wait for a campaign.

say: For example, Grace's church group gets a forward: pregnant women should drink a herbal mixture every morning to prevent all complications. Who says so? No name, no organisation.

panel.heading: Four checks for any health message
items: Who says so?
Does WHO or your clinic agree?
Could it delay care?
Share, correct kindly, or delete

say: Does WHO agree? WHO relies on antenatal contacts and blood pressure checks, not a mixture.

panel.heading: Four checks for any health message
items: Who says so?
Does WHO or your clinic agree?
Could it delay care?
Share, correct kindly, or delete

say: Could it delay care? Yes. A woman who trusts the mixture might ignore a headache or bleeding.

panel.heading: Four checks for any health message
items: Who says so?
Does WHO or your clinic agree?
Could it delay care?
Share, correct kindly, or delete
panel.rule: If it says treat danger signs at home, it is dangerous.

say: Grace replies kindly: thank you for caring, but the safest protection is the eight antenatal contacts, and going to the hospital with any danger sign.

say: Older relatives often hold these beliefs out of love and experience. Thank them, and do not argue.

panel.heading: What people say, what WHO says
left: Give newborns water in the heat
right: Only breast milk for six months
Keep the cord clean and dry

say: Explain the reason simply, and suggest asking the health worker together.
If someone asks which medicine or how much, the answer is always: ask the health worker. And never share someone's health news without permission.

say: Visit or call two facilities. Record travel time day and night, night births with skilled staff, and emergency care such as for heavy bleeding.

say: To remember. Follow the card. Keep the everyday habits, one at a time. Check before you forward, and correct kindly. Send medicine questions to a health worker. And any danger sign means go to a facility now.
